Listen to Shortwave Radio Online Free

Want to listen to shortwave radio online right now, without owning a receiver? You have two options: a live web-based SDR you tune yourself, or our live database showing exactly which stations are broadcasting on-air at this moment.

Option 1: Listen Live via WebSDR

A WebSDR is a real shortwave receiver connected to the internet that anyone can tune remotely, free, in your browser. No account, no software install. We link to three independent receiver networks below — if one is slow or temporarily offline, try another.

How to Listen to International Broadcasts

International shortwave stations — BBC World Service, Radio Romania International, NHK World Japan, and dozens of others — broadcast on published schedules in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time), not your local time zone. That's the single biggest thing to get right before you start: find a station's scheduled hours, convert UTC to your local time, and tune a few minutes early since signals can take a moment to settle in.

If you own a physical receiver, a basic portable with SSB (single sideband) capability, like the ones we've reviewed on the homepage, is enough to pull in most international broadcasters clearly. Reception quality depends heavily on time of day, the band you're tuned to, and your antenna — an external wire antenna dramatically improves weak-signal reception over a stock telescopic whip.

If you don't own a radio yet, WebSDR (above) lets you listen to real international broadcasts immediately, and our schedules by country page organizes stations by where they're broadcasting from, so you can find, say, every station transmitting from Japan or Germany at a glance.

Best Times to Listen

Shortwave propagation changes with the time of day and the ionosphere. Lower bands (49m, 41m, 31m) tend to carry best after dark and into the early morning; higher bands (25m, 19m, 16m) often perform better midday. Our live tracker adjusts automatically — it only shows stations that are actually scheduled to be on air right now.

Can I listen to shortwave radio online for free?

Yes. A WebSDR or KiwiSDR is a real shortwave receiver connected to the internet that you tune in your browser, free, with no account or software. Pick a receiver from the links on this page, tune to a frequency from our schedule, and select AM mode for most broadcasts.

How do I know which shortwave stations are on the air right now?

Shortwave stations broadcast on published schedules in UTC. ShortwaveHQ lists every station scheduled to be on air at the time of the last daily rebuild (see the table above), and the live tracker on the homepage shows current status as you search.

What time zone do shortwave schedules use?

UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). Convert the UTC start time to your local time before you tune in, and tune a few minutes early since signals can take a moment to settle.

What is the best time to listen to shortwave radio?

Lower bands (49m, 41m, 31m) usually carry best after dark and into the early morning; higher bands (25m, 19m, 16m) often perform better during the day. Which band is strongest depends on the time of day, the season and solar conditions.
